cases.name: connection-lifecycle
cases.description: The I/O code chooses a transport and closes connections on every exit path.
cases.prompt: Write an R helper that reads UTF-8 text from a file or URL connection and guarantees cleanup when reading fails.
traps: Leaves an opened connection unclosed after an error
Uses a binary reader for arbitrary text or assumes the caller owns a connection it opened

assertions.text: Registers cleanup immediately after opening a connection.
Makes text encoding explicit and distinguishes text from binary I/O.
States ownership behavior when the caller supplies an existing connection.

cases.name: transport-versus-parsing
cases.description: The answer keeps connection transport separate from schema parsing and project paths.
cases.prompt: A CSV file is read through a compressed connection. Explain which part belongs to connection handling, which belongs to readr, and what tests are needed for non-ASCII data.
traps: Treats the connection as responsible for column types and table schema
Assumes ASCII behavior covers UTF-8 and conversion failures

assertions.text: Separates byte or character transport from delimited-file parsing.
Tests non-ASCII text and encoding conversion explicitly.
Routes paths and artifact ownership to project-layout guidance.
